detailed_rationale:
eClerx Services is a business-process-management, automation and analytics provider to Fortune 2000 enterprises across financial services, communications, retail/fashion, media & entertainment, manufacturing, and travel & leisure - a knowledge-process-outsourcing (KPO) model that skews toward higher-value analytics/automation work rather than pure voice/transaction BPO. FY26 results were genuinely strong: full-year revenue of Rs 4,117 crore (+22% TTM) and net profit of Rs 706 crore (+36% TTM) - profit growing meaningfully faster than revenue, a real sign of operating leverage rather than growth bought at the expense of margin. Operating margin has been stable and healthy at 24-27% across recent quarters (26% in Q4 FY26), and the quant panel's own return metrics confirm this is a high-quality business: ROE ~25.6%, ROCE ~33.7%, both well above the levels typically needed to self-fund growth without diluting shareholders.

The balance sheet is conservatively run (D/E ~0.15x, interest coverage ~25x, borrowings only modestly up to Rs 385 crore from Rs 358 crore), and promoter holding is stable and controlling at 54.53% with no dilution pattern evident. Valuation is moderate rather than cheap or extreme - PE ~23.6-25.4x and ~7.1x book value - which for a business compounding profit at 36% and growing revenue at 22%, with best-in-class return ratios (quality_score 87.7/100, the highest quality reading among this batch of stocks), reads as reasonable rather than stretched. The main data gap in this pass is top-client concentration (locked behind a paywall in available sources) - a real, structural feature of the BPM/KPO business model generally (large enterprise clients tend to represent meaningful revenue shares) that is worth watching even though no specific concentration figure could be confirmed here. No litigation, related-party, or pledge concerns surfaced.
recommendation_rationale: Quant scores this Hold on both windows (53.4 / 59.9), but this is one of the stronger fundamental profiles in this batch - excellent, sustained return ratios, profit growing faster than revenue, stable margins, low leverage, and a valuation that has not run away from the growth. Nothing here argues for anything other than Hold on an existing position (V1 rules do not permit anything more constructive), but among this list this reads as a comparatively high-conviction Hold rather than a marginal one.
summary: eClerx provides higher-value data analytics, automation and process-management services to large global enterprises, and its numbers back up the quality story: profit grew faster than revenue in FY26 (36% vs 22%), margins have stayed healthy and stable, and returns on capital are excellent (ROE ~26%, ROCE ~34%) - all on a reasonably conservative balance sheet and a valuation that is not stretched relative to the growth on offer. The main thing we could not verify in this pass is how concentrated revenue is among its largest clients, a normal feature of this business model worth keeping in view. Overall one of the stronger, more balanced profiles in this review - a Hold, with real quality underpinning it.
positive_para: Profit growing faster than revenue (36% vs 22% TTM) signals genuine operating leverage, not growth purchased with margin give-up; excellent and consistent return ratios (ROE ~25.6%, ROCE ~33.7%) with a 10-year track record of robust ROCE; stable operating margins (24-27%) through multiple quarters; conservative balance sheet (low leverage, high interest coverage) and stable, controlling promoter ownership; valuation (PE ~23-25x) is reasonable relative to the growth and quality on offer, not demanding a leap of faith.
negative_para: Top-client concentration could not be verified in this pass (data behind a paywall) but is a structural feature of the BPM/KPO model worth monitoring - a small number of large enterprise relationships can represent an outsized revenue share. As with any BPM-adjacent business, the 'technical support and digital care' component of the service mix carries some of the same generative-AI/automation disruption exposure that pure-play BPO peers face, even if eClerx's higher-value analytics positioning is likely more defensible than commoditized voice/transaction work; this is a sector-level risk to watch rather than a company-specific weakness observed today. The 36% TTM profit growth rate itself likely includes a temporary operating-leverage catch-up that should not be extrapolated forward at the same pace.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~23-25x trailing earnings for a business compounding profit at well above revenue growth, with ROE near 26% and a clean balance sheet, the multiple looks fair-to-attractive rather than rich - this is close to a reverse-DCF-supported valuation rather than one requiring heroic forward assumptions, provided the current margin and growth trends are not purely cyclical. The main uncertainty is durability: client concentration and the broader AI-disruption question for BPM-adjacent services are real variables that could compress the multiple if either turns adverse, but nothing observed today suggests either is currently a problem.
